citation_verdicts.note: Passage is about harvesting definitions from existing dictionaries and models; it supports the warning the reader draws, not any provenance or authority-ranking claim.
Sentence points to Chapter 3 for the stewardship detail; it names no approving role.
The staging area is explicitly non-persistent; the audit trail is interim and about repository loads, not claim provenance. Supports the row only by analogy.
Supports only the narrow statement that the readiness assessment should include critical business data elements; it says nothing on criteria or designation.

row_verdicts.note: DMBOK2 p733 presents candidate/approved/published/retired as an example of more mature governance and assigns status changes to the governance team. Project covers only the first human gate, so Partial is fair. Both proposal options are legitimate.
Synonyms, conflicting definitions and missing-definition reporting are directly named on pp702-703, with stewards resolving conflicts. Aligned with a citation is fair.
DMBOK2 pp704 and 706 distinguish dictionary, glossary and catalog. README only names the responsibility, so a wording gap is the proportionate reading.

Out of DMBOK scope is not defensible. DMBOK2 Chapter 13 section 2.3 (pdf p781, line 13592) 'Identify Critical Data and Business Rules' gives prioritisation factors (regulatory requirements, financial value, customer impact) and a ranked-list output. The project has no CDE-criteria policy document, which is a real gap the status hides. The reader's own caveat concedes other chapters may cover this, which should have prevented the status. A Partial row proposing criteria be adopted or declined is more honest; 'none' hides the gap.

Intent matches DMBOK2 (metadata managed as versioned data, strategy before products, pp693 and 731). Project has no stated store-of-record per artefact class. The hybrid, centralized and distributed options are fairly drawn from pp708-713. Wording alone might also suffice, but structural-proposal is defensible.

DMBOK2 provenance is about data and metadata, not agent claims. The five-way claim separation is a project addition, so Partial with record-deviation is fair; the deviation is additive rather than contradictory.
pp725-729 match: lineage coverage limits, as-implemented versus as-designed lineage, stitching, and source-forward impact discovery. Only the vocabulary needs sharpening.

Mapping documentation, transformation rules and as-designed lineage are covered (pp696-697, 706, 725). The meaning-survival question is a project framing. Concept-level alignment with a citation is fair; p704 (logical-model meaning lost on deployment) is a closer anchor than the cited passages.

Reader correctly separates the project sense (where evidence may be taken from) from DMBOK2's sense (system of record for a data element). Partial with wording is fair. p734 lists system of record as catalog content, which the reader did not cite.

missing_findings.note: Chapter 13 section 2.3 'Identify Critical Data and Business Rules' gives criteria for critical data (regulatory requirements, financial value, direct customer impact) and says DQ efforts should focus first on critical data. Directly relevant to the missing CDE-criteria policy and contradicts an Out of DMBOK scope status.

Section 6.2 says the master catalog should include 'System of record and other data source statuses'; this supports a system-of-record designation field in catalog or definition artefacts and was not cited.

Section 2.3.3 lists 'Missing Metadata reports' and 'Aging Metadata report' as quality-control activities; relevant to the dictionary and documentation maintenance gap and to the missing-definition findings.

Glossary text says 'Data stewards are generally responsible for glossary development, use, operations, and reporting.' This is a stronger role statement for the human-steward split than the cited p702 lines, and bears on A-09 and A-10.

Lineage coupled with data quality measurements can pinpoint where system design degrades quality, and impact reports support change estimation. Both bear on the lineage completeness and downstream impact duties.
